transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-12
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Record: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Stratify Nexus), Liam O'Neill (Stratify Nexus), Rita Gomez (Stratify Nexus)

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Quick round-robin?
[00:06] Asha: Hi, Asha here, head of cloud partnerships at Stratify Nexus. We run channel for cloud and hardware resells.
[00:10] Liam: Liam, infra lead, focus on onramp/edge and partner integrations.
[00:14] Rita: Rita, channel ops, I manage partner contracts and onboarding.
[00:19] Maya: Great. Diego, want to intro yourself?
[00:21] Diego: Yeah, Diego Ruiz, SE supporting Dedicated and Private deployments, we do a ton of GPU onramp work. Happy to dig into infra details.

--- Quick agenda check ---
[00:35] Maya: Agenda — 1) Partner mechanics & commercial model, 2) basic technical fit: hosting/dedicated/private, 3) security/compliance questions, 4) next steps. Any additions?
[00:43] Asha: Sounds good. We're trying to see how Redwood can sit in our channel catalog — we have customers who want turnkey GPU capacity and partners that resell software bundled.

[01:10] Maya: Perfect. To set context: Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment options. For partners you can either resell hosted credits or become a reseller for Dedicated capacity and private deployments — margins and SLAs differ.
[01:28] Asha: For us, the majority of our deals tilt to on-prem or VPC for regulated industries, but we have SMB customers that want simple hosted access. We need clarity on pricing tiers and partner margins.

[01:46] Diego: On the technical side, capacity for Dedicated is GPU pool-based; we support autoscaling policies, burst, and routing. We also have intelligent prefix/KV cache to reduce per token cost. (note: sometimes Redwood doc transcribes as K-V "cash")
[02:04] Liam: Quick question — for Private/VPC installs, is the control plane fully customer-managed? We need airtight network isolation for a couple of FCA customers.
[02:12] Maya: Yes, Private gives a customer-controlled plane — you can run our runtime inside your VPC or on-prem with an air-gapped option. We do offer KMS integrations and HSM support.
[02:22] Rita: When you say HSM, do you have certified vendors or just generic support? We need to map to our customers' procurement list.
[02:28] Diego: We integrate with major cloud KMS and can plug into customer HSMs; we'll send the compatibility matrix. There's also a SOC2 + ISO attestation summary.

[03:05] Asha: On reseller mechanics — can partners create sub-accounts and allocate commitments? Our channel model needs to provision tenants per reseller and show usage/credits per end-customer.
[03:15] Maya: Yes, there is an organization/sub-org model. Partners can get a reseller account, create sub-accounts, and assign quotas and billing. Clear reporting and token-level cost breakdowns are available in the console.
[03:29] Asha: Is there a self-serve onboarding flow or is it sales-assisted? We want low friction for smaller partners.
[03:33] Maya: There's a self-serve onboarding for hosted tiers; Dedicated and Private usually go through a sales-assisted path because of capacity planning and network setup.

[04:00] Liam: Let's switch to performance: our enterprise clients often ask for predictable p99 latency and throughput for chat workloads. Do you have benchmark numbers?
[04:08] Diego: We maintain perf profiles for curated open models — e.g., 8k context gpt-style model on A100x2 gives median latency X ms (diego's note: numbers were discussed off-record, will share spreadsheet). But — workloads vary a lot by seq len and batching. We can run a pilot to get real numbers on your traffic shape.
[04:28] Asha: Pilot sounds good. We'll want to scope a POC: 6 weeks, two tiered customers, one hosted, one VPC deploy. Is that feasible?
[04:36] Maya: Yes, feasible. Typical pilot has dedicated baseline capacity + sample dataset for quality checks. We'll also include rollout/fallback policies to keep things online if storms hit.

[05:15] Rita: I need to flag procurement — our legal will want a sample reseller addendum and data residency clauses. We also need to see the SLA for Dedicated.
[05:24] Maya: We'll share a sample reseller addendum and the Dedicated SLA. Note that Dedicated SLA depends on committed capacity.

--- Technical deep-dive (abridged) ---
[06:05] Diego: A couple of infra notes — runtime supports kernel selection and quantization-friendly paths. NVlink topology matters for multi-GPU models. For Private setups we recommend minimum nodes with X vGPU (transcript says X as placeholder) and network setup with jumbo frames for KV cache performance.
[06:28] Liam: On network — we prefer private peering, and sometimes customers want air-gap. How intrusive is the agent installation?
[06:34] Diego: The runtime is containerized, we provide helm and systemd options. Air-gapped requires a little prep — offline artifact push and license token. We have an on-prem package we hand to partners.
[06:47] Liam: Any specific kubernetes distro tested? We run mostly K3s at the edge and EKS in cloud.
[06:53] Diego: We certify EKS and GKE; K3s is possible but we treat it case-by-case. We'll need to run compatibility tests.

[08:00] Asha: About margins: what's the typical reseller margin on Hosted vs Dedicated? High level is fine.
[08:07] Maya: Hosted tends to be lower margin but faster revenue; Dedicated has higher margin after committed buys. We'll propose a two-tier margin: self-serve partners vs strategic resellers with volume commit.
[08:20] Rita: Can commission be structured as percent of net revenue or per-commit discounts?
[08:24] Maya: Either is possible. We'll include both structures in the partner deck.

[09:00] Liam: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption in transit and at rest. How deep is the audit log retention?
[09:07] Diego: We expose audit logs to the console and can stream them to customer SIEMs. Retention default is 90 days; longer retention is an add-on.
[09:14] Asha: Is there a SOC2 report we can circulate?
[09:17] Maya: Yes, we'll attach SOC2 report and ISO summary to the follow-up.

[10:30] (ambient cross-talk)
[10:35] Asha: For the pilot customers — compliance will require per-tenant encryption keys and some data residency constraints. Can you support dedicated regions?
[10:42] Maya: We can pin regions for Dedicated and Private. Hosted is multi-region but we can limit endpoints. For per-tenant KMS, we integrate with tenant KMS for Private; for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise customers.

[12:00] Liam: On telemetry — will logs show token-level cost breakdown? That's important for our billing reconciliation.
[12:07] Diego: Yes. Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns. We'll show an example in the follow-up.

[15:00] (Diego shares a quick screen to show partner console prototype — note: transcript imperfectly records visuals)
[15:06] Diego: Here's the partner org view — you can create child orgs, allocate credits, and view usage. There's a simple API for provisioning.
[15:28] Asha: Nice. Do we get programmatic invoice exports?
[15:31] Maya: Yes, CSV exports and API-based billing data are available.

[18:30] Rita: A couple of risk questions from procurement: data deletion guarantees, and audit support for regulators.
[18:41] Maya: Data deletion: for Private you control storage; for Hosted we support data deletion requests and retention policies, with audit logs showing deletion events. We can ship a whitepaper on the process.

[22:00] Asha: Let's talk timeline — partners want onboarding within 4–6 weeks, pilot 6 weeks, production after that. Does that align?
[22:09] Maya: Yes typical timeline: onboarding 2–4 weeks for hosted, 4–8 weeks for Dedicated/private depending on network prep. Pilot 4–8 weeks.

[25:00] Liam: Benchmarks — we'll want a simple test harness. Can Redwood run sample traffic shaped like our customers?
[25:08] Diego: We'll run a bench with your sample prompts. I'll need to know the seq length distribution and concurrency targets; we'll then run the model matrix and share a perf spreadsheet.

[29:00] (brief pause)
[29:10] Asha: On the commercial side, who will handle first-level support for partners?
[29:14] Maya: Redwood provides a partner support tier; for Strategic partners there's dedicated technical onboarding support. Also, we can co-brand a support handbook.

[33:00] Rita: Do you have any reference partners in APAC? We have customers in Singapore and Sydney.
[33:09] Maya: We have a few channel partners in APAC; I'll include a short list and references.

[37:00] Liam: Edge use-cases — some customers want low-latency inference at edge sites. Any constraints?
[37:08] Diego: Edge is possible but typically requires model quantization and smaller footprint models. We can recommend quant profiles and batching configs. Note: audio cut here — Diego said "quant profiles" then the transcript shows "quantize fives" (imperfect).

[41:00] Asha: Contracting — can we get a sample reseller addendum and MSA?
[41:07] Maya: Yes, we'll include sample legal artifacts. For Dedicated, the MSA includes capacity commit terms.

[45:00] (wrap-up)
[45:10] Maya: Recap: share partner deck, sample contracts, SOC2/ISO docs, compatibility matrix, and schedule technical deep-dive. Pilot scoped as hosted + VPC for two customers.
[45:30] Rita: We'll confirm our pilot customers and share their compliance checklist.
[45:40] Asha: Timeline — aim for onboarding week of 3/26?
[45:44] Diego: We're aiming to have bench numbers and deep-dive ready week of 3/19 though.
[46:00] Maya: Okay we'll coordinate dates in follow-up invite.

[53:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-words (K-V "cash", "quantize fives") consistent with live transcription. Deck link: https://redwood.example.com/decks/partner-stratify-intro (internal).
